speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have knee pain after increasing your physical activity. To help me pinpoint the cause, please describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; your age, the recent volleyball activity involving pivoting and twisting, and the worsening pain starting yesterday are very helpful. To narrow this down, does the pain occur specifically when you try to rotate your leg or squat, and is there any swelling or a sensation of the knee giving way?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints). The pain location on the medial tibia, combined with recent increased physical activity and a history of weight loss attempts, strongly points to overuse injury of the tibial bone marrow and surrounding soft tissues.
